subproblem.title: Hausdorff measure of an n-dimensional coordinate box in ℝ^N
subproblem.statement: Let n, N ∈ ℕ, let α : Fin n ↪o Fin N be a strictly increasing multi-index with range A := range α, let c : Fin N → ℝ and let a ≤ b be real numbers. Let B := {x ∈ ℝ^N : c_i + a ≤ x_i ≤ c_i + b for i ∈ A, and x_i = c_i for i ∉ A}. Then μHE[n](B) = (b − a)^n, where μHE[n] is Mathlib's normalized n-dimensional Euclidean Hausdorff measure on ℝ^N (equal to Lebesgue measure on ℝ^n); the equality is stated in [0, ∞] as μHE[n](B) = ENNReal.ofReal((b − a)^n).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n N : ℕ) (α : SimonMultiIndex n N) (c : Fin N → ℝ) (a b : ℝ), a ≤ b → (μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl N)) {x : Eucl N | ∀ i : Fin N, (i ∈ range α → c i + a ≤ x i ∧ x i ≤ c i + b) ∧ (i ∉ range α → x i = c i)} = ENNReal.ofReal ((b - a) ^ n)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 7 of the parent proof ("Measures of faces"), stated for an arbitrary base point c and bounds a ≤ b. With c_i = ρ z_i it gives μHE[n](latticeFace ρ (z, α)) = ρ^n for (a, b) = (0, ρ) (valid as ρ ≥ 0) and μHE[n](K_δ) = (ρ(1 − 2δ))^n for (a, b) = (ρδ, ρ(1 − δ)). Notation: A := range α, B := the set in the statement, x_i := the i-th coordinate of x ∈ ℝ^N.

1. Parametrization. Define ι : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) → ℝ^N by ι(y) := WithLp.toLp 2 (i ↦ c_i + Σ_{j ∈ Fin n} [α(j) = i] · y_j), where [α(j) = i] is 1 if α(j) = i and 0 otherwise. Because α is injective, for j ∈ Fin n exactly one summand of ι(y)_{α(j)} survives, so ι(y)_{α(j)} = c_{α(j)} + y_j; for i ∉ A every summand vanishes, so ι(y)_i = c_i.
2. ι is an isometry. Let y, y' ∈ EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n). By `EuclideanSpace.dist_eq`, dist(ι y, ι y') = sqrt(Σ_{i ∈ Fin N} dist(ι(y)_i, ι(y')_i)²) and dist(y, y') = sqrt(Σ_{j ∈ Fin n} dist(y_j, y'_j)²). In the first sum each term with i ∉ A vanishes (both coordinates equal c_i), so the sum equals the sum over the image α(Fin n) (`Finset.sum_subset`); reindexing along the injective α (`Finset.sum_image`) it becomes Σ_j dist(c_{α(j)} + y_j, c_{α(j)} + y'_j)² = Σ_j dist(y_j, y'_j)² (`dist_add_left`). Hence dist(ι y, ι y') = dist(y, y') for all y, y', i.e. ι is an isometry (`Isometry.of_dist_eq`).
3. ι maps the cube onto B. Let Q := {y ∈ EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) : a ≤ y_j ≤ b for all j}. (⊆) Let y ∈ Q. For i = α(j) ∈ A, ι(y)_i = c_i + y_j ∈ [c_i + a, c_i + b]; for i ∉ A, ι(y)_i = c_i. So ι(y) ∈ B. (⊇) Let x ∈ B and define y ∈ EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) by y_j := x_{α(j)} − c_{α(j)}. The condition of B at the coordinate α(j) ∈ A gives c_{α(j)} + a ≤ x_{α(j)} ≤ c_{α(j)} + b, i.e. a ≤ y_j ≤ b, so y ∈ Q. Moreover ι(y) = x coordinatewise: for i = α(j), ι(y)_i = c_i + (x_i − c_i) = x_i; for i ∉ A, ι(y)_i = c_i = x_i by the condition of B. Hence ι(Q) = B.
4. Transfer to Lebesgue measure. The measure μHE[n] is invariant under isometries (`Isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image`), so μHE[n](B) = μHE[n](ι(Q)) = μHE[n](Q), where on the right μHE[n] is the measure on EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n). On EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n), μHE[n] = volume (`EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume`).
5. Volume of the cube. Q is the preimage of the closed box Icc (fun _ ↦ a) (fun _ ↦ b) ⊆ (Fin n → ℝ) under WithLp.ofLp, and WithLp.ofLp : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) → (Fin n → ℝ) is volume preserving (`PiLp.volume_preserving_ofLp`). The box is measurable, so volume(Q) = volume(Icc (fun _ ↦ a) (fun _ ↦ b)) (`MeasurePreserving.measure_preimage`) = Π_{j ∈ Fin n} ENNReal.ofReal(b − a) (`Real.volume_Icc_pi`) = ENNReal.ofReal(b − a)^n (`Finset.prod_const`, card (Fin n) = n) = ENNReal.ofReal((b − a)^n) (`ENNReal.ofReal_pow`, using b − a ≥ 0, which is where a ≤ b is needed).
6. By steps 4 and 5, μHE[n](B) = ENNReal.ofReal((b − a)^n). (No case split on n is needed; for n = 0, B = {WithLp.toLp 2 c} and Q is the one-point space, both of measure 1.)
proof_key_steps: Parametrize B by ι(y)_i = c_i + Σ_j [α(j) = i] y_j on EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n).
ι is an isometry: coordinates off range α cancel and the rest reindex along the injective α.
ι maps the cube Q = [a, b]^n onto B, with explicit preimage y_j = x_{α(j)} − c_{α(j)}.
Isometry invariance of μHE[n] and μHE[n] = volume on EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) give μHE[n](B) = volume(Q).
volume(Q) = Π_j ofReal(b − a) = ofReal((b − a)^n) via PiLp.volume_preserving_ofLp and Real.volume_Icc_pi.

audit.reason: The type exactly expresses the stated coordinate box and includes a ≤ b. The explicit parametrization is isometric and has precisely the asserted image. Isometry invariance, the pinned Hausdorff normalization and product-box volume give the required ENNReal equality, including n = 0. The proof supplies the needed nonnegativity and measurability facts without depending on another child.

subproblem.title: Coordinate covector dx^α: Kronecker evaluation on coordinate frames and unit coefficient norm
subproblem.statement: Let n, N ∈ ℕ and let α : Fin n ↪o Fin N be a strictly increasing multi-index (SimonMultiIndex n N). Let dx^α := wedgeCovectors n (i ↦ EuclideanSpace.proj (α i)) be the constant n-covector on ℝ^N given by dx^α(v_1, …, v_n) = det[(v_j)_{α(i)}]_{i,j}, and let e_a := EuclideanSpace.single a 1 be the standard basis vectors of ℝ^N. Then (i) dx^α(e_{α(1)}, …, e_{α(n)}) = 1; (ii) dx^α(e_{α'(1)}, …, e_{α'(n)}) = 0 for every multi-index α' : Fin n ↪o Fin N with α' ≠ α; and (iii) covectorEuclideanNorm(c • dx^α) = |c| for every real c, where covectorEuclideanNorm(ω) = (Σ_{I : Fin n → Fin N strictly increasing} ω(e_{I(1)}, …, e_{I(n)})²)^{1/2} is the Euclidean coefficient norm of SimonGMT.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n N : ℕ) (α : SimonMultiIndex n N), (wedgeCovectors n (fun i => EuclideanSpace.proj (α i)) : Covector (Eucl N) n) (fun j => EuclideanSpace.single (α j) (1 : ℝ)) = 1 ∧ (∀ α' : SimonMultiIndex n N, α' ≠ α → (wedgeCovectors n (fun i => EuclideanSpace.proj (α i)) : Covector (Eucl N) n) (fun j => EuclideanSpace.single (α' j) (1 : ℝ)) = 0) ∧ ∀ c : ℝ, covectorEuclideanNorm (c • (wedgeCovectors n (fun i => EuclideanSpace.proj (α i)) : Covector (Eucl N) n)) = |c|
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: steps 1 and 5 of the parent proof (the covector dx^α, its Kronecker evaluation on coordinate frames, and the coefficient-norm computation covectorEuclideanNorm(λ • dx^α) = |λ|), stated for a general degree n. Notation: η := dx^α = wedgeCovectors n (fun i ↦ EuclideanSpace.proj (α i)); e_a := EuclideanSpace.single a (1 : ℝ) ∈ ℝ^N; for I : Fin n → Fin N write e_I := (e_{I(1)}, …, e_{I(n)}).

1. Evaluation formula. Let I : Fin n → Fin N be arbitrary. By `wedgeCovectors_apply_det` (SimonGMT, Chapter06/FormsDuality.lean), η(e_I) = det M_I, where M_I is the n × n real matrix with entries (M_I)_{ij} = proj_{α(i)}(e_{I(j)}) = (e_{I(j)})_{α(i)}. The a-th coordinate of e_b is 1 if a = b and 0 otherwise (`EuclideanSpace.coe_proj`, `PiLp.single_apply`), so (M_I)_{ij} = 1 if α(i) = I(j) and (M_I)_{ij} = 0 otherwise.
2. Proof of the first conjunct. Take I = α (the underlying function of α). Because α is injective, α(i) = α(j) iff i = j (`α.injective.eq_iff`), so (M_α)_{ij} = 1 if i = j and 0 otherwise; that is, M_α is the identity matrix (`Matrix.one_apply`). Hence η(e_{α(1)}, …, e_{α(n)}) = det 1 = 1 (`Matrix.det_one`).
3. Vanishing on the other strictly increasing frames. Let I : Fin n → Fin N be strictly increasing with I ≠ α as functions. Claim: some α(i) ∉ range I. Suppose instead that α(i) ∈ range I for every i, i.e. range α ⊆ range I. Since α and I are injective maps out of Fin n, both ranges are finite sets with exactly n elements (`Set.ncard_range_of_injective`: ncard(range α) = Nat.card (Fin n) = n, and likewise for I); a subset of a finite set having at least as many elements is the whole set (`Set.eq_of_subset_of_ncard_le`), so range α = range I. Two strictly increasing maps out of the well-ordered set Fin n with the same range are equal (`StrictMono.range_inj_of_wellFoundedLT`), so I = α, a contradiction. Fix such an i. For every j, α(i) ≠ I(j) (otherwise α(i) = I(j) ∈ range I), so the whole row i of M_I is zero and det M_I = 0 (`Matrix.det_eq_zero_of_row_eq_zero`). Thus η(e_I) = 0.
4. Proof of the second conjunct. Let α' : Fin n ↪o Fin N with α' ≠ α. Its underlying function I := α' is strictly increasing (`α'.strictMono`), and I ≠ α as functions, because an order embedding is determined by its underlying function (`DFunLike.coe_injective`). By step 3, η(e_{α'(1)}, …, e_{α'(n)}) = η(e_I) = 0.
5. Proof of the third conjunct. Fix c ∈ ℝ. By the definition of covectorEuclideanNorm, covectorEuclideanNorm(c • η) = sqrt(Σ_{I : Fin n → Fin N} s_I), where s_I := ((c • η)(basisFun(I(1)), …, basisFun(I(n))))² if I is strictly increasing and s_I := 0 otherwise. Here basisFun(a) = e_a (`EuclideanSpace.basisFun_apply`) and (c • η)(v) = c · η(v) (`ContinuousAlternatingMap.smul_apply`). We show s_I = (c² if I = α else 0) for every I: (a) if I = α, which is strictly increasing, s_I = (c · 1)² = c² by step 2; (b) if I is strictly increasing and I ≠ α, s_I = (c · 0)² = 0 by step 3; (c) if I is not strictly increasing, then I ≠ α (α is strictly increasing) and s_I = 0 by definition. Hence Σ_I s_I = Σ_I (c² if I = α else 0) = c² (`Finset.sum_ite_eq'`, as α ∈ Finset.univ), and covectorEuclideanNorm(c • η) = sqrt(c²) = |c| (`Real.sqrt_sq_eq_abs`).
6. Steps 2, 4 and 5 are exactly the three conjuncts of the statement. (The argument needs no case split on n: for n = 0, M_I is the empty matrix with determinant 1, Fin 0 → Fin N has the single element α, and step 3 is vacuous.)
proof_key_steps: wedgeCovectors_apply_det: dx^α(e_I) = det M_I with (M_I)_{ij} = 1 if α(i) = I(j), else 0.
I = α: M_α is the identity matrix (α injective), so dx^α(e_α) = 1.
Strictly increasing I ≠ α: equal-size ranges and StrictMono.range_inj_of_wellFoundedLT give some α(i) ∉ range I; that row of M_I is zero, so dx^α(e_I) = 0.
An order embedding α' ≠ α has underlying function ≠ α, so dx^α(e_{α'}) = 0.
In covectorEuclideanNorm(c • dx^α) only the summand I = α survives and contributes c²; sqrt(c²) = |c|.

audit.reason: The prose and exact type agree on all three conjuncts and arbitrary n, N, α and c. The determinant identity, equal-cardinality range argument and zero-row argument establish the frame evaluations. The coefficient-norm sum then has exactly one surviving term c². The proof includes degree zero, is non-circular, and does not rely on the overlapping declaration in another branch.

subproblem.title: Smooth cut-off equal to 1 on a shrunken lattice face and vanishing on all parallel lattice faces
subproblem.statement: Let n, N ∈ ℕ, ρ > 0, δ > 0, z ∈ ℤ^N and let α : Fin n ↪o Fin N be a strictly increasing multi-index with A := range α. Let K := {x ∈ ℝ^N : ρ(z_i + δ) ≤ x_i ≤ ρ(z_i + 1 − δ) for i ∈ A, and x_i = ρ z_i for i ∉ A}. Then there is a C^∞ function φ : ℝ^N → ℝ (ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) φ) with compact support such that 0 ≤ φ ≤ 1 everywhere, φ = 1 on K, and φ = 0 on every lattice face latticeFace ρ (z', α) = ρ(z' + F_α) with z' ∈ ℤ^N, z' ≠ z.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n N : ℕ) (ρ δ : ℝ) (z : Fin N → ℤ) (α : SimonMultiIndex n N), 0 < ρ → 0 < δ → ∃ φ : Eucl N → ℝ, ContDiff ℝ ((⊤ : ℕ∞) : WithTop ℕ∞) φ ∧ HasCompactSupport φ ∧ (∀ x, 0 ≤ φ x ∧ φ x ≤ 1) ∧ (∀ x : Eucl N, (∀ i : Fin N, (i ∈ range α → ρ * ((z i : ℝ) + δ) ≤ x i ∧ x i ≤ ρ * ((z i : ℝ) + 1 - δ)) ∧ (i ∉ range α → x i = ρ * (z i : ℝ))) → φ x = 1) ∧ ∀ z' : Fin N → ℤ, z' ≠ z → ∀ x ∈ latticeFace ρ ((z', α) : LatticeFaceIndex n N), φ x = 0
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: steps 2, 3 and 4 of the parent proof (the boxes K_δ ⊆ int L_δ, the separation of L_δ from every other lattice face of direction α, and the smooth Urysohn cut-off). The bound δ < 1/4 used in the parent is not needed for these steps. Notation: A := range α; x_i is the i-th coordinate of x ∈ ℝ^N, and each coordinate map x ↦ x_i is continuous.

1. The sets. Let L := {x : ρ(z_i + δ/2) ≤ x_i ≤ ρ(z_i + 1 − δ/2) for i ∈ A, |x_i − ρ z_i| ≤ ρ/2 for i ∉ A} and O := {x : ρ(z_i + δ/2) < x_i < ρ(z_i + 1 − δ/2) for i ∈ A, |x_i − ρ z_i| < ρ/2 for i ∉ A}. Each of K, L, O is the intersection over i ∈ Fin N of the set defined by its condition at the coordinate i. If i ∈ A, that set is the intersection of the two half-spaces {x : t ≤ x_i} and {x : x_i ≤ t'} (closed for K and L) or {x : t < x_i} and {x : x_i < t'} (open for O). If i ∉ A, it is the hyperplane {x : x_i = ρ z_i} (closed, for K), the slab {x : |x_i − ρ z_i| ≤ ρ/2} (closed, for L), or the slab {x : |x_i − ρ z_i| < ρ/2} (open, for O). Hence K and L are closed (`isClosed_iInter`) and O, a finite intersection of open sets, is open (`isOpen_iInter_of_finite`).
2. K ⊆ interior L. Clearly O ⊆ L. Let x ∈ K. For i ∈ A, using ρ > 0 and δ > 0: ρ(z_i + δ/2) < ρ(z_i + δ) ≤ x_i ≤ ρ(z_i + 1 − δ) < ρ(z_i + 1 − δ/2). For i ∉ A: |x_i − ρ z_i| = 0 < ρ/2. So K ⊆ O. As O is open and O ⊆ L, O ⊆ interior L (`interior_maximal`); hence K ⊆ interior L.
3. L is compact. Let x ∈ L. For i ∈ A, ρ z_i − ρ ≤ ρ z_i ≤ ρ(z_i + δ/2) ≤ x_i ≤ ρ(z_i + 1 − δ/2) ≤ ρ z_i + ρ; for i ∉ A, |x_i − ρ z_i| ≤ ρ/2 ≤ ρ. Hence L ⊆ toLp(Π_{i ∈ Fin N} [ρ z_i − ρ, ρ z_i + ρ]), the image of a compact product of closed intervals (`isCompact_univ_pi`, `isCompact_Icc`) under the continuous map WithLp.toLp 2 : (Fin N → ℝ) → ℝ^N (`PiLp.continuous_toLp`); this image is compact. A closed subset of a compact set is compact (`IsCompact.of_isClosed_subset`), so L is compact.
4. Smooth Urysohn function. The space ℝ^N, as a smooth manifold modelled on itself (model 𝓘(ℝ, ℝ^N)), is finite-dimensional, Hausdorff, normal and σ-compact. Apply Mathlib's `exists_contMDiffMap_one_nhds_of_subset_interior` with smoothness exponent ⊤ : ℕ∞, s := K (closed by step 1) and t := L, using K ⊆ interior L (step 2). It gives a map f : ℝ^N → ℝ, C^∞ in the manifold sense, such that f = 1 on a neighbourhood of K (in particular f(x) = 1 for every x ∈ K, `Filter.Eventually.self_of_nhdsSet`), f(x) = 0 for every x ∉ L, and f(x) ∈ [0, 1] for every x. Let φ := f. By `contMDiff_iff_contDiff`, φ is ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞); also 0 ≤ φ ≤ 1 everywhere and φ = 1 on K.
5. Compact support. φ vanishes outside the compact set L (steps 3 and 4), so HasCompactSupport φ (`HasCompactSupport.intro`).
6. Vanishing on the other faces of direction α. Let z' ∈ ℤ^N with z' ≠ z and x ∈ latticeFace ρ (z', α); by definition ρ z'_i ≤ x_i ≤ ρ(z'_i + 1) for i ∈ A and x_i = ρ z'_i for i ∉ A. We show x ∉ L, whence φ(x) = 0 by step 4. Choose i with z'_i ≠ z_i (`Function.ne_iff`). Since z'_i and z_i are distinct integers, z'_i + 1 ≤ z_i or z_i + 1 ≤ z'_i. (a) If i ∈ A and z'_i + 1 ≤ z_i, then x_i ≤ ρ(z'_i + 1) ≤ ρ z_i < ρ(z_i + δ/2), violating the lower bound in the definition of L at i. (b) If i ∈ A and z_i + 1 ≤ z'_i, then x_i ≥ ρ z'_i ≥ ρ(z_i + 1) > ρ(z_i + 1 − δ/2), violating the upper bound of L at i. (c) If i ∉ A, then x_i = ρ z'_i and |x_i − ρ z_i| = ρ |z'_i − z_i| ≥ ρ > ρ/2, because |z'_i − z_i| ≥ 1 for distinct integers (`Int.one_le_abs`); this violates the condition of L at i. In all cases x ∉ L, so φ(x) = 0.
7. Steps 4, 5 and 6 give a function φ with all the required properties.
proof_key_steps: Enlarged box L (margins δ/2 along range α, transversal slab of half-width ρ/2) and open box O; K and L are closed, O is open.
K ⊆ O ⊆ L, hence K ⊆ interior L.
L lies in a compact product box (via WithLp.toLp) and is closed, hence compact.
Smooth Urysohn (exists_contMDiffMap_one_nhds_of_subset_interior with exponent ⊤ : ℕ∞, then contMDiff_iff_contDiff): 0 ≤ φ ≤ 1, φ = 1 on K, φ = 0 off L, so φ has compact support.
Every point of latticeFace ρ (z', α), z' ≠ z, violates the L-condition at a coordinate where z' and z differ, so φ vanishes there.

audit.reason: The type matches every cutoff property and both positivity hypotheses. Its explicitly coerced smoothness order denotes C∞, not analyticity. The proof establishes closedness, K ⊆ interior L, compactness of L, smooth Urysohn applicability and separation from every other parallel face. No upper bound on δ is needed; the argument remains valid when K is empty and in degree zero.

subproblem.title: Mass-admissible test form isolating one lattice face
subproblem.statement: Let n, N ∈ ℕ, ρ > 0, 0 < δ < 1/4 and F₀ ∈ LatticeFaceIndex n N (an n-face ρ(z + F_α) of the cubical lattice 𝓛_n(ρ) in ℝ^N). Then there is a test form ω ∈ TestFormOn univ n (a C^∞ compactly supported n-form on ℝ^N) which is mass-admissible (ω ∈ massAdmissibleOn univ n univ, i.e. tsupport ω ⊆ univ and covectorEuclideanNorm(ω(x)) ≤ 1 for all x), satisfies [[F]](ω) = latticeFaceAction ρ F ω = 0 for every face index F ≠ F₀, and satisfies (ρ(1 − 2δ))^n ≤ [[F₀]](ω).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n N : ℕ) (ρ δ : ℝ) (F₀ : LatticeFaceIndex n N), 0 < ρ → 0 < δ → δ < 1 / 4 → ∃ ω : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Eucl N)) n, ω ∈ massAdmissibleOn (univ : Set (Eucl N)) n univ ∧ (∀ F : LatticeFaceIndex n N, F ≠ F₀ → latticeFaceAction ρ F (ω : DifferentialForm (Eucl N) n) = 0) ∧ (ρ * (1 - 2 * δ)) ^ n ≤ latticeFaceAction ρ F₀ (ω : DifferentialForm (Eucl N) n)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: steps 5, 6 (the vanishing of each [[F]](ω) for F ≠ F₀; the lattice sum itself is left to the parent) and 8 of the parent proof, together with the F₀-specific parts of steps 2 and 7, taken with the sign s := 1; the parent's assembly recovers the sign by using ω or −ω. Parent step 1 is supplied by the sibling coord_covector, steps 2–4 by face_cutoff and step 7 by box_measure. Notation: write F₀ = (z, α) with z ∈ ℤ^N and α : Fin n ↪o Fin N; A := range α; e_a := EuclideanSpace.single a (1 : ℝ); for a face index F = (z', α'), latticeFaceAction ρ F ω = ∫_{latticeFace ρ F} ω(x)(e_{α'(1)}, …, e_{α'(n)}) dμHE[n](x).

1. Ingredients. Let η := wedgeCovectors n (fun i ↦ EuclideanSpace.proj (α i)). By coord_covector: η(e_{α(1)}, …, e_{α(n)}) = 1; η(e_{α'(1)}, …, e_{α'(n)}) = 0 for every α' : Fin n ↪o Fin N with α' ≠ α; and covectorEuclideanNorm(c • η) = |c| for every real c. By face_cutoff, applied to n, N, ρ, δ, z, α (it uses only ρ > 0 and δ > 0), there is φ : ℝ^N → ℝ with ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) φ, HasCompactSupport φ, 0 ≤ φ(x) ≤ 1 for all x, φ(x) = 1 for all x ∈ K := {x : ρ(z_i + δ) ≤ x_i ≤ ρ(z_i + 1 − δ) for i ∈ A, x_i = ρ z_i for i ∉ A}, and φ(x) = 0 for all x ∈ latticeFace ρ (z', α) whenever z' ≠ z.
2. The test form. Let ω₀(x) := φ(x) • η. It is C^∞ of order (⊤ : ℕ∞), as the product of the smooth scalar function φ with a constant covector (`ContDiff.smul` with `contDiff_const`), so ω₀ is a smooth form (IsSmoothForm means ContDiff ℝ ∞ with ∞ = (⊤ : ℕ∞)); its support lies in the support of φ, so it has compact support (`HasCompactSupport.smul_right`); and tsupport ω₀ ⊆ univ trivially. Hence ω₀ ∈ TestFormOn univ n; let ω be this element. For all x and all v : Fin n → ℝ^N, ω(x)(v) = φ(x) · η(v).
3. Admissibility. tsupport ω ⊆ univ, and for every x, covectorEuclideanNorm(ω(x)) = covectorEuclideanNorm(φ(x) • η) = |φ(x)| = φ(x) ≤ 1 by step 1 and 0 ≤ φ(x) ≤ 1. Hence ω ∈ massAdmissibleOn univ n univ.
4. Faces F ≠ F₀ contribute 0. Let F = (z', α') with F ≠ F₀. Case α' ≠ α: for every x the integrand is ω(x)(e_{α'(1)}, …, e_{α'(n)}) = φ(x) · 0 = 0 (step 1), so latticeFaceAction ρ F ω = ∫ 0 = 0 (`integral_zero`). Case α' = α: then z' ≠ z (otherwise F = (z, α) = F₀), and for every x ∈ latticeFace ρ (z', α) the integrand is φ(x) · η(e_{α(1)}, …, e_{α(n)}) = 0 · 1 = 0 by step 1; a set integral of a function vanishing on the set is 0 (`setIntegral_eq_zero_of_forall_eq_zero`). In both cases latticeFaceAction ρ F ω = 0.
5. The F₀ term. For every x, ω(x)(e_{α(1)}, …, e_{α(n)}) = φ(x) · 1 = φ(x), so latticeFaceAction ρ F₀ ω = ∫_{latticeFace ρ F₀} φ dμHE[n].
6. Two measures, from box_measure with c_i := ρ z_i. For i ∈ A, the condition ρ z_i ≤ x_i ≤ ρ(z_i + 1) is equivalent to c_i + 0 ≤ x_i ≤ c_i + ρ, and for i ∉ A both sets require x_i = c_i; so latticeFace ρ F₀ is the box of box_measure with (a, b) = (0, ρ), 0 ≤ ρ, and μHE[n](latticeFace ρ F₀) = ENNReal.ofReal(ρ^n) < ∞. Similarly ρ(z_i + δ) ≤ x_i ≤ ρ(z_i + 1 − δ) is equivalent to c_i + ρδ ≤ x_i ≤ c_i + ρ(1 − δ), and ρδ ≤ ρ(1 − δ) because δ < 1/4 < 1/2 and ρ > 0; so box_measure gives μHE[n](K) = ENNReal.ofReal((ρ(1 − δ) − ρδ)^n) = ENNReal.ofReal((ρ(1 − 2δ))^n).
7. Inclusion, measurability, integrability. K ⊆ latticeFace ρ F₀: for i ∈ A, ρ z_i ≤ ρ(z_i + δ) ≤ x_i ≤ ρ(z_i + 1 − δ) ≤ ρ(z_i + 1) (ρ > 0, δ > 0), and for i ∉ A the conditions coincide. K is closed, being the intersection over i of closed half-spaces (i ∈ A) or closed hyperplanes (i ∉ A) in the continuous coordinates x ↦ x_i; hence K is measurable. φ is continuous (it is C^∞), hence a.e. strongly measurable, and |φ| ≤ 1; since μHE[n](latticeFace ρ F₀) < ∞ (step 6), φ is integrable on latticeFace ρ F₀ (`Measure.integrableOn_of_bounded`).
8. Lower bound. Since ρ > 0 and 1 − 2δ > 0, the real number (ρ(1 − 2δ))^n is ≥ 0, so (ρ(1 − 2δ))^n = μHE[n](K).toReal (step 6, `ENNReal.toReal_ofReal`) = ∫_K 1 dμHE[n] (`setIntegral_const`) = ∫_K φ dμHE[n] (φ = 1 on the measurable set K, `setIntegral_congr_fun`) ≤ ∫_{latticeFace ρ F₀} φ dμHE[n] (`setIntegral_mono_set`: φ is integrable on latticeFace ρ F₀, φ ≥ 0 there, and K ⊆ latticeFace ρ F₀) = latticeFaceAction ρ F₀ ω (step 5).
9. Steps 2, 3, 4 and 8 show that ω has all the required properties.
proof_key_steps: Take η = dx^α (coord_covector) and the cut-off φ for (z, α, δ) (face_cutoff), where F₀ = (z, α).
ω := φ • η is a C^∞ compactly supported form, and covectorEuclideanNorm(φ(x) • η) = φ(x) ≤ 1 makes it mass-admissible.
Faces with α' ≠ α see η(e_{α'}) = 0; faces (z', α) with z' ≠ z see φ = 0; so [[F]](ω) = 0 for every F ≠ F₀.
[[F₀]](ω) = ∫_{F₀} φ dμHE[n]; box_measure gives μHE[n](F₀) = ρ^n < ∞ and μHE[n](K) = (ρ(1 − 2δ))^n.
φ is integrable on F₀, φ ≥ 0, φ = 1 on the closed set K ⊆ F₀, hence [[F₀]](ω) ≥ μHE[n](K) = (ρ(1 − 2δ))^n.

audit.reason: The exact type matches admissibility, off-face vanishing and the quantitative lower bound. The proof uses precisely its three declared dependencies to construct φ • dx^α. It explicitly establishes finite face measure, integrability, measurable K, nonnegativity and integral comparison. It is complete and non-circular. Its conclusion implies the selected parent via tsum_eq_single, the admissible forms ±ω, le_massOn and continuity as δ approaches zero from above.
